policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV DEU.5.10 reads 'them that love me and keep my commandments' — a first-person suffix matching the qere מִצְוֺתָי ('my commandments'), in a clause where God speaks in the first person ('love me'). The ketiv מצותו carries a third-person suffix ('his commandments'), which the ASV's 'my' excludes. The only note on the verse ('Or, a thousand generations') is an alternative_rendering touching 'thousands' and does not bear on this unit.
